newsitem.title: CANADA: ELAN, Gibson get Alberta pipe approval.
newsitem.headline: ELAN, Gibson get Alberta pipe approval.

text.p: ELAN Energy Inc and Gibson Petroleum Co Ltd said on Wednesday they received regulatory approval for their planned 55,000 barrel per day heavy oil pipeline in Alberta.
Construction of the 150 km line, called the ECHO pipeline, is expected to start in October. The anticipated startup is early next year, the companies said.
The pipeline was designed to move heavy crude oil to Hardisty, Alberta from the Elk Point area, site of ELAN producing fields.
At Hardisty, the raw heavy oil will be blended to downstream export specifications, they said.

The companies said the 12-inch pipeline would be insulated to allow the movement of hot oil, eliminating the need for diluent. Diluent, made up of light hydrocarbons, is commonly mixed with heavy oil to aid in pipeline transport.
ELAN said the ECHO pipeline would be the first in western Canada to use the technology, which is aimed at allowing more flexibility in oil marketing than with blended oil streams.
ELAN's current production from the Elk Point area is about 22,000 barrels per day (16,000 net to the company).
